section_summary: This section contains three 1937 consular despatches concerning Chinese labor migration through Dairen into Manchuria. The first two provide quarterly statistics, discuss labor shortages and immigration quotas, and include tables organized by embarkation port; the third announces suspension of the reports after local authorities classified the figures as military secrets. A final 1933 departmental note comments on a despatch about the Grand Manchurian Exposition.

subfiles.title: Chinese Coolie Immigration and Emigration Through Dairen, First Quarter of 1937
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador at Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports Chinese labor arrivals and departures through Dairen during the first quarter of 1937.
subfiles.summary: The despatch describes the seasonal increase in Chinese laborers entering Manchuria and records 65,902 arrivals through Dairen during the quarter. It discusses reported labor shortages associated with Manchuria's Five-Year Plan and proposals to increase both the general immigration quota and the quota for building-trade workers. The enclosure tabulates migration by embarkation port and provides annual arrival, departure, and net-increase figures for 1931–1936.

subfiles.title: Chinese Coolie Immigration and Emigration Through Dairen, Second Quarter of 1937
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador at Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports Chinese labor migration through Dairen during April–June 1937 and analyzes labor demand in Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Seasonal immigration reached its height in May and declined in June after most agricultural workers had arrived. The report records 61,622 arrivals and 29,589 departures, notes that Dairen handled an estimated 40 percent of laborers entering Manchuria, and discusses continuing labor shortages and rumors of a higher immigration quota. Its enclosure breaks down arrivals and departures by port and reproduces annual totals for 1931–1936.

subfiles.title: Temporary Discontinuance of Quarterly Reports on Chinese Coolie Immigration and Emigration Through Dairen
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador at Tokyo
subfiles.about: Announces the suspension of quarterly migration reports after Dairen authorities classified the underlying statistics as military secrets.
subfiles.summary: The Dairen Police Bureau refused to provide the customary third-quarter migration figures because they were now considered militarily sensitive, and the consulate judged press reports incomplete or unreliable. Grummon suggests that unusually large numbers of laborers had returned to China, producing a shortage of stevedores at a time when hostilities had greatly increased shipping. The resulting congestion left foreign commercial vessels waiting outside Dairen harbor for several days, alongside numerous transports.

subfiles.title: Departmental Note on the Grand Manchurian Exposition
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Comments on an August 22, 1933, Dairen despatch describing the Grand Manchurian Exposition.
subfiles.summary: The note characterizes the exposition itself as relatively unimportant. It nevertheless recommends reading the despatch because it illustrates an interesting method used for educational purposes.
